title: Canonical refinement restriction and integral domain inclusion
statement: Use the pro-etale coefficient systems, derived inverse/direct images and open extension of [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data]. For a coefficient system $R$, a scheme map $f:X\to Y$, compactifications $c,d$ and a refinement $r:c\to d$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], suppose the pullback coefficient map along $rj_c=j_d$ equals the composite of the maps along $r$ and $j_c$. For an ordinary derived $R_X$-module $M$, define the refinement restriction $j_d^*Rr_*j_{c!}M\to j_c^*j_{c!}M$ as the pullback-composition identification followed by $j_c^*$ of the derived adjunction counit $r^*Rr_*\to1$. Independently, for a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and any scheme $W$, define the functor from $D^b_{ctf}(W,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] to the derived-complete bounded constructible integral category by forgetting only the uniform finite-Tor condition, leaving every underlying object and arrow unchanged. Finally, for a finite-field datum $D$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and $\ell\ne D.p$, retain the proved canonical witness that the image of $\ell$ in $D.k$ is a unit. No absolute separatedness, finite-type hypothesis, refinement invertibility or coefficient-comparison theorem is part of these constructions.

def refinementRestriction (R : Coefficients.{u})
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} {c d : Compactification f} (r : c.Refinement d)
    (hc : R.pull (c.i ≫ r.hom) = proEtaleRingCompositeCoefficients c.i r.hom
      (R.ring d.Z) (R.ring c.Z) (R.ring X) (R.pull r.hom) (R.pull c.i))
    (M : DerivedCategory (pbcModules X (R.ring X))) :
    (pull R d.i).obj ((push R r.hom).obj
        ((openExtension R c.i).mapDerivedCategory.obj M)) ⟶
      (pull R c.i).obj ((openExtension R c.i).mapDerivedCategory.obj M)
